The child who only wants snacks

One look at the snack basket and your little one's eyes go wide. A single plate is never enough, so they keep asking for more — and then, at the dinner table, they hang their head and say they're too full to eat.

"That's enough" only sounds unfair to a child. But when a story shows them why they should save room for dinner, they start wanting to manage the snacks themselves.

content.alt: 06. Just This Much Snack, Meals Come First! - Why managing snacks matters
content.text:
Why managing snacks matters

The toddler years are when eating rhythms take shape, so the habit of snacking in moderation and eating meals on time becomes the foundation of healthy growth. When snacks fill the tummy all the way up, there's simply no room left for dinner.

What children need isn't a rule that says "just hold back," but a simple principle: one plate of snacks, only at a set time. When they manage that small act of self-control on their own, they also discover the joy of how much tastier food is when the meal comes first.

content.alt: 06. Just This Much Snack, Meals Come First! - The story of Kongi's snack basket
content.text:
The story of Kongi's snack basket

In 『Just This Much Snack, Meals Come First!』, Kongi can't resist and secretly empties the whole snack basket. By evening his tummy is stuffed and aching, and even with his favorite dinner in front of him he can't take a single bite.

As Mom rubs his tummy and tells him a story, the tummy becomes a little room. The next day, Kongi eats just this much and sets the plate right back down. Holding back was hard at first, but he did it! By dinnertime his tummy is rumbling — food tastes this good?

content.alt: 06. Just This Much Snack, Meals Come First! - Snack rules to practice at home
content.text:
Snack rules to practice at home

Once you've read the story, it's time to put it into practice at home. Here are a few ways to start.

First, decide on the snack portion together. Serve it on one plate and show them "this much" with their own eyes so the amount is easy to picture. Second, set a rule that snacks happen only at a set time. The order — meal first, snack later — becomes second nature. Third, praise them warmly when they hold back. Recognizing the courage it took to set the plate down turns self-control into a proud accomplishment.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How many snacks are just the right amount?

A. It's best to serve just this much — a set portion — so it doesn't spoil their appetite for meals. When a story teaches the order of meals before snacks, children accept it naturally.

Q. What should I do when my child begs for snacks?

A. Agreeing on the time and the amount in advance, then sticking to it consistently, really helps. Let a toddler snack habit storybook show them naturally that a good meal means more energy for play.

Q. How do I choose healthy snacks?

A. Small portions of snacks that complement meals, like fruit or dairy, work well. Praising your child when they stick to the right amount on their own turns it into a lasting snack habit.
